Hi Anna — thanks for the clear list. Brief answers up front, and we can follow up with artifacts & a call: 

1) Hosted API (Redwood public API): we do NOT use customer prompts/responses to continuously train our foundation or hosted catalog models by default. We have a strictly opt-in telemetry program used for aggregate performance tuning (customers must explicitly opt in from the Console or via contract). If a customer opts out, that setting is honored immediately for new traffic; any prior opt-in data used for tuning is excluded from future training cycles going forward.

2) Dedicated & Private: by design, Dedicated capacity is isolated — Redwood does not train on customer data from Dedicated pools. Private (VPC / on-prem) deployments are customer-managed and Redwood does not have access to prompts/responses unless configured by the customer (e.g., for managed-support debugging). In all cases, training on customer content requires explicit contractual agreement.

3) Subprocessors: I'll attach our current subprocessor registry and a short attestation note confirming that subprocessors who handle prompt data are contractually bound to our no-train/no-derive obligations and encryption/KMS controls. If subprocessors process data outside the EU we rely on SCCs or customer-specific transfer mechanisms; we'll flag any EEA-cross-border subprocessors in the registry.

4) We'll provide a redacted audit-log sample, SOC 2 Type II cover pages (full report under NDA), and our SIG self-assessment / CAIQ export where available.

Next steps: Marissa (Privacy) and Rishi (Legal) are cc'd and will share the formal artifacts and the redacted log. Can we tentatively book a 30-minute slot Thursday 16:00–16:30 PT (we can also do Friday morning)?
